text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Annual flooding in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta has killed 44 people so far while 11 others are missing following a whirlwind storm which struck at the weekend.
-- The central State Bank has no plans to devalue the Vietnamese dong and is introducing measures to stabilise the exchange rate.
-- A Vatican delegation is due to arrive today for a five-day visit.
-- Flooding has killed 20 children, inundated more than 100,000 houses and caused damage worth 354.7 million VND ($32.2 million) in An Giang province, on the border with Cambodia.
-- Vietnam is investing 295 billion VND ($26.9 million) to develop the country's teacher-training system.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's Party Committee has held a meeting to discuss concerns over industrial modernisation, corruption and rising migration from neighbouring provinces.
-- Seven people have been killed, two seriously injured and four are reported missing following a flash-flood in the northern mountain province of Ha Giang.
-- The government has issued a new directive on financial management and accounting systems at state-owned enterprises to ensure their financial independence.
-- Some 170,000 students and pupils in Hanoi's Dong Da district took part in an anti-drug programme on Sunday.
-- The government has set up a committee to oversee the management of rural development and irrigation systems in Vietnam's Mekong Delta.
